chunks: From him, from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the mu'talah (mutual divorce for compensation), it was said: her waiting period is the same as that of the divorced woman, and she observes it in her house; and the mu'talah is in the position of the mubar'ah (divorce by mutual agreement).

key_terms.المُبَارِئَةِ: Mutual divorce where both parties agree to separate, often without specified compensation
key_terms.المُخْتَلِعَةِ: A woman who divorces herself by paying compensation to her husband (Khul/Mu'talah)
key_terms.عِدَّةَ الْمُطَلَّقَةِ: The waiting period of a divorced woman

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and legal status of a woman in a Khul (mutual compensation) divorce according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar*, clarifying that the *mukhla'ah* (wife-initiated divorce) follows the *iddah* of a revocable divorce (*raj'i*), emphasizing her residence in her marital home during the waiting period. The comparison to *mubar'ah* highlights the procedural similarity in dissolving the bond, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding financial compensation and finality. This hadith underscores the legal symmetry between different forms of divorce initiated by the wife, ensuring consistent observance of the waiting period to ascertain lineage and readiness for remarriage.
